Main.sentence: John Fitzgerald Kennedy (May 29, 1917 – November 22, 1963), also known as JFK , was the 35th ___E:president of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ , serving from 1961 until ___E:his assassination U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_John_F._Kennedy)___ in 1963. He was the ___E:youngest U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_the_United_States_by_age)___ person ___E:elected U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_presidential_election)___ president at 43 years. [a] Kennedy served at the height of the ___E:Cold War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War)___ , and the majority of his foreign policy concerned relations with the ___E:Soviet Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union)___ and ___E:Cuba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba)___ .

A member of the ___E:Democratic Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States))___ , Kennedy represented ___E:Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts)___ in both houses of the ___E:United States Congress U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress)___ before his presidency.

Born into the prominent ___E:Kennedy family U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_family)___ in ___E:Brookline, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brookline,_Massachusetts)___ , Kennedy graduated from ___E:Harvard University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_University)___ in 1940, joining the ___E:U.S. Naval Reserve U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Naval_Reserve)___ the following year. During ___E:World War II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II)___ , he commanded ___E:PT boats U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PT_boat)___ in the ___E:Pacific theater U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_War)___ .

Kennedy's survival following the sinking of PT-109 and his rescue of his fellow sailors made him a war hero and earned the ___E:Navy and Marine Corps Medal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navy_and_Marine_Corps_Medal)___ , but left him with serious injuries.

After a brief stint in journalism, Kennedy represented ___E:a working-class Boston district U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts%27s_11th_congressional_district)___ in the ___E:U.S. House of Representatives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._House_of_Representatives)___ from 1947 to 1953. He was subsequently elected to the ___E:U.S. Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Senate)___ , serving as the junior ___E:senator for Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_senators_from_Massachusetts)___ from 1953 to 1960. While in the Senate, Kennedy published his book Profiles in Courage , which won a ___E:Pulitzer Prize U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulitzer_Prize_for_Biography_or_Autobiography)___ .
Kennedy ran in the ___E:1960 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_1960_presidential_campaign)___ .

His campaign gained momentum after ___E:the first televised presidential debates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1960_United_States_presidential_debates)___ in American history, and he was elected president, narrowly defeating ___E:Republican U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ opponent ___E:Richard Nixon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon)___ , the incumbent vice president.

Kennedy's presidency saw high tensions with communist states in the Cold War. He increased the number of ___E:American military advisers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_advisor#US_advisors_in_Vietnam)___ in ___E:South Vietnam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Vietnam)___ , and the ___E:Strategic Hamlet Program U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strategic_Hamlet_Program)___ began during his presidency.

In 1961, he authorized attempts to overthrow the Cuban government of ___E:Fidel Castro U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fidel_Castro)___ in the failed ___E:Bay of Pigs Invasion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bay_of_Pigs_Invasion)___ and ___E:Operation Mongoose U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Mongoose)___ .

In October 1962, U.S. spy planes discovered Soviet missile bases had been deployed in Cuba. The resulting period of tensions, termed the ___E:Cuban Missile Crisis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_Missile_Crisis)___ , nearly resulted in ___E:nuclear war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_war)___ .

In August 1961, after ___E:East German U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Germany)___ troops erected the ___E:Berlin Wall U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Wall)___ , Kennedy sent an army convoy to reassure West Berliners of U.S. support, and delivered ___E:one of his most famous speeches U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ich_bin_ein_Berliner)___ in West Berlin in June 1963. In 1963, Kennedy signed the first ___E:nuclear weapons treaty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partial_Nuclear_Test_Ban_Treaty)___ .

He presided over the establishment of the ___E:Peace Corps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peace_Corps)___ , ___E:Alliance for Progress U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alliance_for_Progress)___ with Latin America, and the continuation of the ___E:Apollo program U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_program)___ with the goal of ___E:landing a man on the Moon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_choose_to_go_to_the_Moon)___ before 1970. He supported the ___E:civil rights movement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_rights_movement)___ but was only somewhat successful in passing his ___E:New Frontier U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Frontier)___ domestic policies.
On November 22, 1963, Kennedy was assassinated in ___E:Dallas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas)___ .

His vice president, ___E:Lyndon B. Johnson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon_B._Johnson)___ , ___E:assumed the presidency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_inauguration_of_Lyndon_B._Johnson)___ . ___E:Lee Harvey Oswald U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Harvey_Oswald)___ was arrested for the assassination, but he was shot and killed by ___E:Jack Ruby U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Ruby)___ two days later.

The ___E:Federal Bureau of Investigation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Bureau_of_Investigation)___ (FBI) and the ___E:Warren Commission U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Commission)___ both concluded Oswald had acted alone, but ___E:conspiracy theories about the assassination U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination_conspiracy_theories)___ persist.

After Kennedy's death, Congress enacted many of his proposals, including the ___E:Civil Rights Act of 1964 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_Rights_Act_of_1964)___ and the ___E:Revenue Act of 1964 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revenue_Act_of_1964)___ .
Kennedy ranks highly in ___E:polls of U.S. presidents U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_rankings_of_presidents_of_the_United_States)___ with historians and the general public.

His personal life has been the focus of considerable sustained interest following public revelations in the 1970s of his chronic health ailments and ___E:extramarital affairs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extramarital_affair)___ .
Kennedy is the most recent ___E:U.S. president to have died in office U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_the_United_States_who_died_in_office)___ .

John Fitzgerald Kennedy was born outside ___E:Boston U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston)___ in ___E:Brookline, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brookline,_Massachusetts)___ , on May 29, 1917,  to ___E:Joseph P. Kennedy Sr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_P._Kennedy_Sr.)___ , a businessman and politician, and ___E:Rose Kennedy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose_Kennedy)___ ( ___E:née U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N%C3%A9e)___ Fitzgerald), a philanthropist and socialite.

His paternal grandfather, ___E:P. J. Kennedy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P._J._Kennedy)___ , was an East Boston ___E:ward boss U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_boss)___ and ___E:Massachusetts state legislator U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts_Senate)___ .

Kennedy's maternal grandfather and namesake, ___E:John F. Fitzgerald U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Fitzgerald)___ , was a U.S. congressman and two-term ___E:mayor of Boston U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor_of_Boston)___ .
All four of his grandparents were children of Irish immigrants.

Kennedy had an older brother, ___E:Joseph Jr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_P._Kennedy_Jr.)___ , and seven younger siblings: ___E:Rosemary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosemary_Kennedy)___ , ___E:Kathleen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathleen_Kennedy_Cavendish)___ , ___E:Eunice U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eunice_Kennedy_Shriver)___ , ___E:Patricia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patricia_Kennedy_Lawford)___ , ___E:Robert U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy)___ , ___E:Jean U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Kennedy_Smith)___ , and ___E:Ted U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Kennedy)___ .
Kennedy's father amassed a private fortune and established ___E:trust funds U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trust_funds)___ for his nine children, guaranteeing them lifelong financial independence.
His business kept him away from home for long stretches, but Joe Sr. was a formidable presence in his children's lives.
He encouraged them to be ambitious, emphasized political discussions at the dinner table, and demanded a high level of academic achievement.

John's first exposure to politics came in ___E:1922 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1922_Massachusetts_gubernatorial_election)___ , when he toured ___E:Boston wards U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neighborhoods_in_Boston)___ with his grandfather Fitzgerald during his unsuccessful gubernatorial campaign.

In September 1927, due to an outbreak of ___E:polio U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polio)___ in ___E:Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts)___ and Joe Sr.'s business interests in ___E:Wall Street U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wall_Street)___ and ___E:Hollywood U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_the_United_States)___ , the family relocated from Boston to the ___E:Riverdale U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale,_Bronx)___ neighborhood of New York City.   Several years later, his brother Robert told ___E:Look U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Look_(American_magazine))___ magazine that his father left Boston because of job signs that read: " ___E:No Irish Need Apply U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Irish_Need_Apply)___ ."  The Kennedys spent summers and early autumns at ___E:their home U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Compound)___ in ___E:Hyannis Port, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyannis_Port,_Massachusetts)___ , a village on ___E:Cape Cod U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Cod)___ ,  where they engaged in various outdoor activities.

Christmas and Easter holidays were spent at their ___E:winter retreat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Querida_(mansion))___ in ___E:Palm Beach, Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Beach,_Florida)___ .

In September 1930, Kennedy, 13 years old, was sent to the ___E:Canterbury School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canterbury_School_(Connecticut))___ in ___E:New Milford, Connecticut U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Milford,_Connecticut)___ , for 8th grade.
In April 1931, he had an ___E:appendectomy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appendectomy)___ , after which he withdrew from Canterbury and recuperated at home.

In September 1931, Kennedy began attending ___E:Choate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choate_Rosemary_Hall)___ , a preparatory boarding school in ___E:Wallingford, Connecticut U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wallingford,_Connecticut)___ .

Rose had wanted John and Joe Jr. to attend a ___E:Catholic school U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_school)___ , but Joe Sr. believed that if they were to compete in the political world, they needed to be among boys from prominent ___E:Protestant U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestantism)___ families.
John spent his first years at Choate in his older brother's shadow and compensated with rebellious behavior that attracted a clique.
Their most notorious stunt was exploding a toilet seat with a firecracker.

In the next chapel assembly, the headmaster, George St. John, brandished the toilet seat and spoke of "muckers" who would "spit in our sea," leading Kennedy to name his group "The Muckers Club." It included his roommate and lifelong friend ___E:Lem Billings U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lem_Billings)___ .
Kennedy graduated from Choate in June 1935, finishing 64th of 112 students.
He had been the business manager of the school yearbook and was voted the "most likely to succeed."

Kennedy intended to study under ___E:Harold Laski U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harold_Laski)___ at the ___E:London School of Economics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_School_of_Economics)___ , as his older brother had done. However, ill health forced his return to the United States in October 1935, when he enrolled late at ___E:Princeton University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princeton_University)___ , but had to withdraw after two months due to gastrointestinal illness.
In September 1936, Kennedy enrolled at ___E:Harvard College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_College)___ .

He wrote occasionally for The Harvard Crimson , the campus newspaper, but had little involvement with campus politics, preferring to concentrate on athletics and his social life. Kennedy played ___E:football U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football)___ and was on the junior varsity squad during his sophomore year, but an injury forced him off the team, and left him with back problems that plagued him for the rest of his life. He earned membership in the ___E:Hasty Pudding Club U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasty_Pudding_Club)___ and the ___E:Spee Club U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spee_Club_(Harvard))___ , one of Harvard's elite " ___E:final clubs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_College_social_clubs#Origins)___ ".

In July 1938, Kennedy sailed overseas with his older brother to work at the ___E:American embassy in London U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Embassy,_London)___ , where their father was serving as President ___E:Franklin D. Roosevelt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_D._Roosevelt)___ 's ambassador to the ___E:Court of St. James's U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Court_of_St._James%27s)___ .

The following year, Kennedy traveled throughout Europe, the ___E:Soviet Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union)___ , the ___E:Balkans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balkans)___ , and the Middle East in preparation for his Harvard senior honors thesis.

He then went to Berlin, where a U.S. diplomatic representative gave him a secret message about war breaking out soon to pass on to his father, and to ___E:Czechoslovakia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czechoslovakia)___ before returning to London on September 1, 1939—the day that ___E:Germany invaded Poland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Poland)___ ; the start of ___E:World War II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II)___ .
Two days later, the family was in the ___E:House of Commons U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_House_of_Commons)___ for speeches endorsing the United Kingdom's declaration of war on Germany.

Kennedy was sent as his father's representative to assist with arrangements for American survivors of the torpedoing of ___E:SS Athenia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS_Athenia_(1922))___ before flying back to the United States on his first transatlantic flight.
While an upperclassman at Harvard, Kennedy began to take his studies more seriously and developed an interest in ___E:political philosophy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_philosophy)___ .

He made the ___E:dean's list U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dean%27s_list)___ in his junior year.  In 1940, Kennedy completed his thesis, "Appeasement in Munich", about British negotiations during the ___E:Munich Agreement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munich_Agreement)___ .
The thesis was released on July 24, under the title Why England Slept .
The book was one of the first to offer information about the war and its origins, and quickly became a bestseller.

In addition to addressing Britain's unwillingness to strengthen its military in the lead-up to the war, the book called for an ___E:Anglo-American alliance U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anglo-American_alliance)___ against the rising totalitarian powers.
Kennedy became increasingly supportive of U.S. intervention in World War II, and his father's isolationist beliefs resulted in the latter's dismissal as ambassador.
In 1940, Kennedy graduated cum laude from Harvard with a Bachelor of Arts in government, concentrating on ___E:international affairs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_affairs)___ .

That fall, he enrolled at the ___E:Stanford Graduate School of Business U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanford_Graduate_School_of_Business)___ and audited classes,  but he left after a semester to help his father complete his memoirs as an American ambassador.
In early 1941, Kennedy toured South America.
Kennedy planned to attend ___E:Yale Law School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yale_Law_School)___ , but canceled those plans when American entry into World War II seemed imminent.
In 1940, Kennedy attempted to enter the Army's ___E:Officer Candidate School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_Candidate_School_(United_States_Army))___ .
Despite months of training, he was medically disqualified due to chronic back problems.

On September 24, 1941, with the help of ___E:Alan Goodrich Kirk U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Goodrich_Kirk)___ —the director of the ___E:Office of Naval Intelligence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_of_Naval_Intelligence)___ (ONI) and former naval ___E:attaché U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attach%C3%A9)___ to Joe Sr.—Kennedy joined the ___E:United States Naval Reserve U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Naval_Reserve)___ .
He was commissioned as an ___E:ensign U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ensign_(rank))___ on October 26, 1941,  and joined the ONI staff in Washington, D.C.

In January 1942, Kennedy was assigned to the ONI field office at Headquarters, ___E:Sixth Naval District U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sixth_Naval_District)___ , in ___E:Charleston, South Carolina U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charleston,_South_Carolina)___ .

He hoped to command a ___E:PT (patrol torpedo) boat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PT_boat)___ , but his health problems seemed almost certain to prevent active duty. Kennedy's father intervened by providing misleading medical records and convincing PT officers that his presence would bring publicity to the fleet.

Kennedy completed six months of training at the ___E:Naval Reserve Officer Training School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Reserve_Officer_Training_School)___ in Chicago and at the ___E:Motor Torpedo Boat Squadrons Training Center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motor_Torpedo_Boat_Squadrons_Training_Center)___ in ___E:Melville, Rhode Island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melville,_Rhode_Island)___ .

His first command was PT-101 from December 7, 1942, until February 23, 1943.  Unhappy with his assignment to the ___E:Panama Canal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panama_Canal)___ , far from the fighting, Kennedy appealed to Senator ___E:David Walsh U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_I._Walsh)___ of Massachusetts, who arranged for him to be reassigned to the ___E:South Pacific U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Theater_(World_War_II))___ .

In April 1943, Kennedy was assigned to Motor Torpedo Squadron TWO,  and on April 24 he took command of PT-109 ,  then based on ___E:Tulagi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulagi)___ Island in the ___E:Solomons U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solomon_Islands)___ .

On the night of August 1–2, in support of the ___E:New Georgia campaign U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Georgia_campaign)___ , PT-109 and fourteen other PTs were ordered to block or repel four Japanese destroyers and floatplanes carrying food, supplies, and 900 Japanese soldiers to the Vila Plantation garrison on the southern tip of the Solomon's ___E:Kolombangara U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolombangara)___ Island.

Intelligence had been sent to Kennedy's commander, Thomas G. Warfield, who, as a result, was expecting the arrival of the large Japanese naval force that would pass on the evening of August 1. Of the 24 torpedoes fired that night by eight of the American PTs, not one hit the Japanese convoy.

On that moonless night, Kennedy spotted a Japanese destroyer heading north on its return from the base of Kolombangara around 2:00 a.m., and attempted to turn to attack, when PT-109 was suddenly rammed at an angle and cut in half by the ___E:destroyer Amagiri U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_destroyer_Amagiri_(1930))___ , killing two PT-109 crew members.    [b] Avoiding surrender, the remaining crew swam toward ___E:Plum Pudding Island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plum_Pudding_Island)___ , 3.5 miles (5.6 km) southwest of the remains of PT-109 , on August 2.   Despite re-injuring his back in the collision, Kennedy towed a badly burned crewman named Patrick McMahon  to the island with a life jacket strap clenched between his teeth.

From there, Kennedy and his subordinate, Ensign George Ross, made forays through the coral islands, searching for help.  When they encountered an English-speaking native with a canoe, Kennedy carved his location on a ___E:coconut U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coconut)___ shell and requested a boat rescue.
Seven days after the collision, with the coconut message delivered, the PT-109 crew was rescued.
Almost immediately, the PT-109 rescue became a highly publicized event.
The story was chronicled by John Hersey in The New Yorker in 1944; decades later, it was the basis of a successful ___E:film U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PT_109_(film))___ .
It followed Kennedy into politics and provided a strong foundation for his appeal as a leader.

Hersey portrayed Kennedy as a modest, self-deprecating hero.  For his courage and leadership, Kennedy was awarded the ___E:Navy and Marine Corps Medal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navy_and_Marine_Corps_Medal)___ , and the injuries he suffered during the incident qualified him for a ___E:Purple Heart U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purple_Heart)___ .
After a month's recovery, Kennedy returned to duty, commanding PT-59 .
On November 2, Kennedy's PT-59 , along with two other PT boats, took part in the rescue of 40 to 50 Marines.

The 59 acted as a shield from shore fire as they escaped on two rescue landing craft at the base of the Warrior River on ___E:Choiseul Island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raid_on_Choiseul)___ , taking ten Marines aboard and delivering them to safety.
Under doctor's orders, Kennedy was relieved of his command on November 18, and sent to the hospital on Tulagi.

By December 1943, with his health deteriorating, Kennedy left the Pacific front and arrived in San Francisco in early January 1944.  After receiving treatment for his back injury at the ___E:Chelsea Naval Hospital U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Naval_Hospital)___ in Massachusetts from May to December 1944, he was released from active duty.   Beginning in January 1945, Kennedy spent three months recovering from his back injury at ___E:Castle Hot Springs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castle_Hot_Springs_(Arizona))___ , a resort and temporary military hospital in Arizona.
On March 1, 1945, Kennedy retired from the Navy Reserve on physical disability and was honorably discharged with the full rank of lieutenant.
When later asked how he became a war hero, Kennedy joked: "It was easy. They cut my PT boat in half."
